question: Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats meet at________ hills.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nilgiri.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Nilgiri Hills are located at the junction of the **Western Ghats** and **Eastern Ghats** in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Kerala.
 
• The popular hill station Ooty (Udhagamandalam), also known as the "**Queen of Hill Stations**," is situated in the Nilgiri Hills.
 
• The Nilgiri Hills are part of the Western Ghats, recognized as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** and a biodiversity hotspot with rich flora and fauna.
 
• The Nilgiri region is famous for its **tea plantations**, producing a significant portion of India's tea, which is a key economic activity here.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Shivalik Hills:**

 
• The Shivalik Hills, also known as the **Outer Himalayas**, are the lowest range of the Himalayan mountain system, stretching from Jammu and Kashmir to Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• They are composed of unconsolidated sediments brought down by rivers, making them prone to erosion and landslides.

**Maikal Hills:**

 
• The Maikal Hills are part of the **Satpura Range**, located in central India, mainly in Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
 
• This region is known for its dense forests and is home to several tribal communities, including the **Gond **and **Baiga tribes**.

**Amarkantak Hills:**

 
• Amarkantak Hills are the origin point of major rivers like the **Narmada** and **Son** rivers.
 
• Amarkantak is a popular religious and **pilgrimage** site, known for its scenic beauty and religious significance in Hinduism.
